bga_name: Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory
rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Action Phase 2 Common Actions 3 Working Class 3.1 Basic Actions 3.2 Free Actions 4 Middle Class 4.1 Basic Actions 4.2 Free Actions 5 Capitalist Class 5.1 Basic Actions 5.2 Free Actions 6 State 6.1 Basic Actions 6.2 Free Actions Action Phase During the action phase, players take actions in turn, in increasing status order (Working Class, Middle Class, Capitalist Class, State). Every time it’s your turn, you must play a card. For your Main Action , you may take either the action on the card or a Basic Action of your choice as listed in the next section. If you cannot take the action on the card, you may still use the card for a Basic Action. As well as the basic action, you may take a single Free Action in your turn. This can be before or after your Main Action, but it cannot be in the middle. You cannot pass. There should be no reason to, as basic actions such as Apply Political Pressure are always of benefit to you. The action phase continues until each player has taken 5 actions. This should mean they have 2 cards remaining in their hand. The table below summarises the basic and free actions available to each class. Common Actions Every class has a common basic action: Propose a Bill: You take one Bill marker and place it on a desired, adjacent policy section where do not already have a marker. You may also spend 1 Influence to call an Immediate Vote for the proposed Bill. Every class has a common free action: Paying Off Loan: You spend 50 Vardis (50 money) to discard a Loan. Working Class Basic Actions Apply Political Pressure: You may add 3 voting cubes to the Bag. Assign Workers: You can choose up to 3 of your non-committed Workers from anywhere on the board, place them in available Companies, and commit them. Buy Resources (Goods & Services): You can choose a single good or service and buy from up to two sources as many tokens as your current population per source. Strike: You can place a Strike token on up to two Companies, which prevents them from producing. Demonstration: You can place a Demonstration token in the Unemployed Workers area if the number of unemployed workers is at least 2 higher than available Working Class worker slots. Free Actions Claim Benefits: You can receive the benefits that the State has placed in the appropriate State Benefits boxes. Swap Workers: You may swap any number of a skilled worker with an unskilled worker without affecting their commitment in Companies. Spend Healthcare equal to population, to gain 1 Prosperity, gain VP according to prosperity track slot and extra 2VP, then received an unskilled worker in the Unemployed Worker area. Spend Education equal to population, to gain 1 Prosperity, gain VP according to prosperity track slot, then Upgrade one of your unskilled workers anywhere on the board to a skilled one. You may change the color of a skilled worker instead. Spend Luxury equal to population, to gain 1 Prosperity, gain VP according to prosperity track slot. Middle Class Basic Actions Apply Political Pressure: (As above). Assign Workers: (As above). Buy Resources (Goods & Services): You can choose a single good or service and buy tokens up to your current population, and you also have the ability to buy for free from yourself by transferring goods from Storages to Goods & Services. Build Company: You can pay for a Company from the Market, which you MUST have all the required non-committed MC workers from anywhere on the board. WC-employees need not be available. Set wages within Policy 2, assign and commit MC workers. If available, you may also assign and commit WC worker. Sell Company: You can discard one of your Companies that currently has no committed Workers to gain revenue equal to the Company's cost. Export Resources (Sell to Foreign Market): You can perform any or all available transactions for either Food or Luxury a maximum of one time. Only allowed to sell from Storages. Gain 1 VP for every transaction. Extra Shift: You can choose a Company with non-committed Middle Class workers, commit them, and produce goods. Free Actions Adjust Prices: You can change the prices of goods on your player board. Adjust Wages: You can adjust the wages in any of your Companies abiding by Policy 2, though raising wages commits workers and you cannot lower wages of already committed workers. Claim Benefits: (As above). Swap Workers: (As above). Spend Healthcare equal to population: (As above). Spend Education equal to population: (As above). Spend Luxury equal to population: (As above). Capitalist Class Basic Actions Apply Political Pressure: (As above). Build Company: Choose and pay for a Company from the Market. Place Company on the board and set wages within Policy 2. If available, you may commit and assign Workers from the Unemployed Workers area to fully staff company. Sell Company: You can discard one of your Companies that currently has no committed Workers to gain revenue equal to the Company's cost. Export Resources (Sell to Foreign Market): You can perform any or all available transactions a maximum of one time. Lobbying: You can spend 30 Vardis (30 money) from your Capital to gain 3 Influence. Business Deal: You can choose one of the Business Deals, pay the cost, and receive the goods in either your Storages (paying tax according to Policy 6) or the Free Trade Zone (no tax needed to pay). Free Actions Adjust Prices: (As above). Adjust Wages: You can adjust the wages in any of your Companies abiding by Policy 2. Buy Storage: You can pay 20 for an extra Storage and dedicate it to a single resource. Pay Bonus: You can choose one of your operational Companies, pay 5 Vardis (5 Money) to the workers, and commit those workers. State Basic Actions Export Resources (Sell to Foreign Market): You are only allowed to sell either Food or Luxury Goods in State player board, perform any or all available transactions at a maximum of one time. Event Action: You can perform the specific task outlined on an Event Card. [Tips: PROVIDE : use what you have or buy the required resource(s) and put it in the appropriate State Benefits boxes; SPEND : spend from what you have to Supply]. Meet with MPs: You give 2 Personal Influence (in State Player Board) to a player and move their corresponding Legitimacy marker one space forward. Extra Tax: You get 10 Vardis from each player, then get -1 Legitimacy to the two classes with the lowest Legitimacy score (choose if tied). Players need to take Loan if unable to pay. Campaign: You can convert up to 3 Media Influence (Main Board) into Personal Influence (State Player Board). Free Actions Adjust Wages: You can adjust the wages in any of your Companies, abiding by Policy 2. [Passive Benefit: You automatically receive 1 VP whenever another player uses the Claim/Receive Benefits action.]

[Rating: 1/10] economy and politics simulation strategy game somewhat asymmetric  Not sure about the theme. It's different and a bit interesting, but it reminds too much of daily problems and work. I also don't fully believe in the Class Conflict, especially not as a fixed inescapable truth.  I like the card-driven play (play a card for effect or discard for basic action) and that the cards have a slight 'epic event feel'. [Rating: 1/10] Well done simulation of Capitalism. Not a board game, because no room for decisions, 5 turn long pre-destined and random card trigger game.  CAUTION! This game is just overhyped at this moment. If the hype upvoters are done, the real value of the game will drop to around 40$ and have a score of 6.9-7.2. Only recommended for Finance and Economist students.

[Rating: 1/10] A silly, pointless game. Blah. I don’t even enjoy computer games like this and at least in those I don’t have to do all the tedious management of game pieces, mechanics. Blah

[Rating: 1/10] Note due au travail de localisationde Don't Panic Games... ou plutôt l'absence de travail, le nombres d'erreurs qui impactent le jeu est assez colossale... Ce que je peux tolérer, projet trop ambitieux pour l'éditeur -à la limite- mais l'absence de communication alors que présents sur un fil dédié à ces erratas... non.   Sinon pour le jeu c'est un solide 9/10:  De ces jeux qu'on éspère pouvoir sortir régulièrment, malgré la lourdeur du monstre.  Très didactique et globalement cohérent, avec Twillight Struggle ou Gigawatt des jeux superbes même en temps qu'outils de connaissances et compréhensi

[Rating: 1/10] Erreurs sur la VF qui rendent le jeu injouable. L'éditeur a décidé de proposer un pack de correction payant en septembre ! Honteux.

[Rating: 1/10] Fun to play once or twice. It's long due to how much bloat it has. Very good at feeling like an economy sim and less like a game with economy in it. Play once or twice then it's done.  Update: Played a third time on BGA. This is not a game for me. Its well made and the mechanisms and simulation are genuinely fun, but the time it takes to actually get through everything is insane. If anyone in your group has AP then steer clear.   Update 2: I have been roped into a fourth time. This is not even a game. I just did a bunch of random junk and won. Its also heavily dependant on what cards you draw.

[Rating: 1/10] Another asymmetric euro game where everybody's too tired to look at the other boards, too exhausted to talk. So nothing interesting happens.

Still, I couldn’t help but notice its meteoric rise in BGG’s ratings and some friends raved about it, so my desire to play it was very high. After I did, I can only say Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory is a crushing disappointment to me.  • I like the theme; Hegemony throws you into the heart of a class struggle.
